- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). content.content:
## Loan Analyzer

Interactive loan comparison tool built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Recharts.

It lets you compare multiple loans side‑by‑side, visualize amortization, and export/share the results.

## Tech stack

- Next.js (App Router)
- React + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS 4
- Recharts

## Getting started

```bash
# install deps
npm install

# run dev server
npm run dev

# build for production
npm run build

# run production build
npm start
```

Then open `http://localhost:3000` in your browser.

## Environment & deployment

This app is designed to work without any secrets committed to the repo.

If you add environment variables (e.g. analytics keys, third‑party APIs), put them in a `.env.local` file that is **not** committed to git. The `.gitignore` is already configured to ignore common `.env*` files.

The production instance currently lives at `https://loananalyzer.parthchovatiya.tech`.

## License

This project is licensed under the MIT License. See `LICENSE` for details.
---NOTE---
- Export to PDF
-------------------------------------------------------------------
- “Best Strategy Recommendation” (AI Advisor)
⚡ Recommendation
If you prepay ₹3L in year 3, you will save ₹8,20,000 in interest
and reduce the loan tenure by 4 years.

Your current interest rate is 9.5%.
Average market rate is 8.1%.

Refinancing could save ₹6,40,000.

-------------------------------------------------------------------

Loan Health Score: 72 / 100

Based on:
	•	interest rate vs market
	•	loan tenure
	•	prepayment history
	•	debt-to-income ratio

Then suggest improvements.

People love scores.

-------------------------------------------------------------------

Smart Notifications

📢 You can save ₹1.8L interest if you prepay ₹50k this year

📉 RBI reduced repo rate.
You may qualify for lower interest rate.

-------------------------------------------------------------------

Multi-Loan Strategy Planner

Many people have multiple loans:
	•	home loan
	•	personal loan
	•	credit card
	•	car loan

Let them prioritize payoff strategy.

Example strategies:
	•	Avalanche (highest interest first)
	•	Snowball (smallest loan first)

Show payoff timeline.


-------------------------------------------------------------------

Loan Payoff Countdown

🏁 Loan Free Date
15 July 2042

With progress bar.
People love tracking progress.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------------
----------------------------------------------------------------------NEXTCONFIG---
import type { NextConfig } from 'next';

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  headers: async () => [
    {
      source: '/(.*)',
      headers: [
        { key: 'X-Content-Type-Options', value: 'nosniff' },
        { key: 'X-Frame-Options', value: 'DENY' },
        { key: 'X-XSS-Protection', value: '1; mode=block' },
        { key: 'Referrer-Policy', value: 'origin-when-cross-origin' },
        {
          key: 'Permissions-Policy',
          value: 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()',
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
};

export default nextConfig;
---ENV---
OPENAI_API_KEY=<redacted>

## Loan Analyzer

Interactive loan comparison tool built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Recharts.

It lets you compare multiple loans side‑by‑side, visualize amortization, and export/share the results.

## Tech stack

- Next.js (App Router)
- React + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS 4
- Recharts

## Getting started

```bash
# install deps
npm install

# run dev server
npm run dev

# build for production
npm run build

# run production build
npm start
```

Then open `http://localhost:3000` in your browser.

## Environment & deployment

This app is designed to work without any secrets committed to the repo.

If you add environment variables (e.g. analytics keys, third‑party APIs), put them in a `.env.local` file that is **not** committed to git. The `.gitignore` is already configured to ignore common `.env*` files.

The production instance currently lives at `https://loananalyzer.parthchovatiya.tech`.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev            # Next.js dev server at http://localhost:3000
npm run build          # Production build
npm start              # Serve production build
npm run lint           # ESLint (flat config, eslint.config.js)
npm run format         # Prettier write over src/**/*.{ts,tsx,css}
npm run format:check   # Prettier check (CI-safe)
```

There is no test runner configured in this repo.

## Environment

- `OPENAI_API_KEY` (in `.env.local`, gitignored) — required by `/api/chat` and `/api/recommend` is pure-compute (no key). The chat and intent-detection calls use `gpt-4o-mini`.
- App runs without secrets for everything except the AI chat feature.

## Architecture

Next.js 15 App Router + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS 4 + Recharts. The app is a **client-side single-page tool** with three thin API routes for tasks that can't run in the browser.

### The amortization engine is the single source of truth

`src/utils/amortization.ts` (`calculateAmortization`) is the core. Every feature — charts, summary cards, recommendations, the AI chat, and the PDF — derives its numbers from this one function. When touching loan math, change it here; do not recompute loan figures elsewhere.

Domain is **Indian reducing-balance EMI loans**: pre-payments are applied to principal *before* interest is computed for that month (see the comment at amortization.ts:83); amounts are formatted in lakhs/crores (₹). `generateSummary` (`src/utils/summary.ts`) wraps the engine to produce `withPrePayments` vs `withoutPrePayments` results plus interest/months saved.

### Rendering path

`src/app/page.tsx` (server) → `client-app.tsx` (`'use client'`) → `src/App.tsx`. `App.tsx` is the real root component holding all UI state and orchestrating hooks. Note `src/App.tsx` lives outside `src/app/` — it's the legacy component root from a pre-Next.js (Vite) structure. The `dist/` folder is a stale Vite build artifact and is not part of the Next.js build.

### State & persistence

No backend database. All loan state lives in React via `useLoanData` (`src/hooks/useLoanData.ts`) and is debounce-persisted to `localStorage` under key `loan-analyser-state` (`src/utils/storage.ts`). The "What-If Simulator" keeps a separate `plannedPPs` state in `App.tsx` that is merged with real pre-payments only for simulated views.

### Data flow layers

- `src/types/` — shared domain types (`loan.ts` is central: `LoanInput`, `PrePayment`, `RateChange`, `AmortizationRow/Result`, `LoanSummary`).
- `src/utils/` — pure functions: amortization, summary, validation, formatters, and `chatContext.ts` (builds the enriched LLM context + what-if scenario computation).
- `src/hooks/` — stateful glue (`useAmortization`, `useRecommendations`, `useExportPdf`, `useChat`, `useLoanData`).
- `src/services/recommendations/` — strategy generators (prepayment, emi-increase, lump-sum) combined and ranked by `interestSaved` in `index.ts`.
- `src/components/` — UI, with `charts/` (Recharts) and `pdf/` subfolders.

### API routes (`src/app/api/`)

- `recommend/route.ts` — validates loan, calls `getRecommendations`, returns ranked strategies. Pure compute, no external calls.
- `chat/route.ts` — OpenAI chat. Pattern: detect what-if intent (`hasWhatIfKeywords` → `detectScenarioIntent` LLM classify → `computeScenario` via the local engine), inject **pre-computed** numbers into the system prompt, then stream the response as SSE. The LLM is explicitly instructed never to do its own math — it only narrates engine output.
- `export-pdf/route.ts` — server-rendered PDF via `puppeteer-core`. Uses a locally-detected Chrome in `development` and `@sparticuz/chromium` in production (serverless). HTML comes from `export-pdf/template.ts`. `maxDuration = 30`.

## Conventions

- Path alias `@/*` → `src/*` (tsconfig). Components/hooks under `src/` often use relative imports; API routes and utils use `@/`.
- TypeScript `strict` is on. Keep loan calculations immutable and centralized in the engine.
- Security headers are set globally in `next.config.ts`.

Perfect! Now I have comprehensive information. Let me compile the complete inventory report:

## Complete Loan Analyser Analytics & Features Inventory

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's a comprehensive inventory of existing analytics, charts, insights, and the owner's feature wishlist:

---

### 1. EXISTING CHART COMPONENTS

Located in: `/Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/charts/`

| Chart | Visualization | Data/Props |
|-------|---|---|
| **BalanceChart.tsx** | Outstanding loan balance over time (line chart) | Takes `LoanSummary` + optional `simulatedResult`; displays closing balance month-by-month; supports comparison with simulated scenario |
| **PrincipalInterestChart.tsx** | Principal vs Interest composition per EMI (stacked bar chart) | Takes `AmortizationRow[]` schedule; samples data for large schedules to keep readable; shows principal (green) + interest (red) breakdown per month |
| **CumulativeInterestChart.tsx** | Cumulative interest paid over loan tenure (area chart) | Takes `LoanSummary` + optional `simulatedResult`; builds running total of interest; supports dual-line comparison (actual vs simulated) |
| **YearlySummaryChart.tsx** | Yearly principal + interest aggregation (stacked bar chart) | Takes `AmortizationRow[]` schedule; groups by year; shows total principal repaid + prepayments vs interest per year |
| **PaymentBreakupChart.tsx** | Total principal vs total interest as percentage (pie/donut chart) | Takes `LoanSummary`; displays final split with percentages; legend shows absolute amounts in currency |
| **ComparisonChart.tsx** | Actual vs Simulated scenario comparison (bar chart with custom patterns) | Takes `LoanSummary` + optional `simulatedResult`; side-by-side bars for each scenario; custom tooltip & legend formatting |

---

### 2. SUMMARY & INSIGHT COMPONENTS

**SummaryCards.tsx** (`/src/components/SummaryCards.tsx`)
Currently displays 8 metric cards:
- Total Interest (with tooltip "total interest over entire loan tenure after pre-payments")
- Interest Saved (% reduction vs original)
- Closure Date (estimated loan end date)
- Months Saved (EMI months cut from tenure)
- Total Paid (principal + interest + all pre-payments)
- Effective Cost (multiple of borrowed amount, e.g., 1.50x)
- Interest Ratio (interest as % of principal)
- Progress (% of principal repaid based on current date, with progress bar)

**RecommendationPanel.tsx** (`/src/components/RecommendationPanel.tsx`)
- Displays 3 strategy recommendations (fetched from API)
- Each recommendation shows type (Prepayment/EMI Increase/Lump Sum), title, description, priority badge
- Impact metrics: interest saved, months saved
- Refresh button to re-fetch recommendations

**WhatIfSimulator.tsx** (`/src/components/WhatIfSimulator.tsx`)
- Allows users to add planned prepayments (date + amount)
- Shows simulated impact with 4 metrics:
  - Interest Saved (from simulated vs current)
  - Months Reduced (fewer months of EMI)
  - New Closure Date
  - ROI (interest saved per rupee invested)

---

### 3. CORE DATA MODEL

**AmortizationRow** (`/src/types/loan.ts`)
```
- month: number
- date: string (YYYY-MM-DD)
- openingBalance: number
- interestComponent: number (interest for that month)
- principalComponent: number (principal portion of EMI)
- prePayment: number (any lump sum prepayment)
- totalPayment: number (EMI + prepayment)
- closingBalance: number (remaining outstanding)
- annualRate: number (effective rate for that month)
```

**AmortizationResult** (`/src/types/loan.ts`)
```
- schedule: AmortizationRow[]
- totalInterest: number
- totalAmountPaid: number
- closureDate: string (estimated loan end date)
- totalMonths: number (loan tenure in months)
```

**LoanSummary** (`/src/types/loan.ts`)
```
- withPrePayments: AmortizationResult (schedule after pre-payments)
- withoutPrePayments: AmortizationResult (baseline without pre-payments)
- interestSaved: number (difference in total interest)
- monthsSaved: number (difference in tenure)
```

**LoanInput** (user inputs)
```
- id, principal, annualRate, emi, emiDebitDay (1-28), startDate
```

---

### 4. DERIVED METRICS & COMPUTATION ENGINE

**File:** `/src/utils/amortization.ts` & `/src/utils/summary.ts`

**Currently Computed:**
- `totalInterest` — aggregate interest across all months
- `totalAmountPaid` — principal + interest + all prepayments
- `closureDate` — date when outstanding balance reaches zero
- `totalMonths` — number of EMI payments (loan duration)
- `interestSaved` — comparison of with-prepayment vs baseline interest
- `monthsSaved` — comparison of with-prepayment vs baseline tenure
- `principalComponent` per month (derived from EMI - interest)
- `closingBalance` per month (cumulative principal reduction)
- **Rate changes:** system tracks effective annual rate per month
- **Prepayment handling:** pre-payments reduce principal BEFORE interest calculation (Indian mortgage model)

**Useful Metrics NOT Yet Derived/Shown:**
- **Loan Health Score** (mentioned in note.txt; would need: interest rate vs market, tenure, prepayment history, debt-to-income ratio)
- **Payoff countdown** (days/weeks/months until loan closure from today)
- **Average monthly interest** (helps users understand per-month cost)
- **Interest burden ratio** (interest paid per year as % of annual income or EMI)
- **Breakeven point** (month where principal > interest in EMI)
- **Savings trajectory** (how much total interest will be saved if X rupees prepaid annually)
- **Rate sensitivity analysis** (if rate increases by 0.5%, what's impact on tenure/interest)
- **Seasonal prepayment insights** (e.g., "if you bonus ₹5L in March, you save ₹X")

---

### 5. RECOMMENDATION SERVICES

**File:** `/src/services/recommendations/`

**Three Strategy Engines:**

1. **Prepayment Strategy** (`prepayment.ts`)
   - Tests 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% of current balance as one-time prepayment in year 1
   - Returns best option with interest saved + months saved + new closure date
   - Priority: high/medium/low based on interest saved

2. **EMI Increase Strategy** (`emi-increase.ts`)
   - Tests 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% increase to current EMI
   - Shows impact on tenure reduction and interest saved
   - Validates that modified EMI is feasible

3. **Lump Sum Timing Strategy** (`lump-sum.ts`)
   - Recommends paying 2x EMI immediately
   - Emphasizes "earlier is always better" principle
   - Shows months/interest saved

**Recommendation Interface:**
```
- id, type, title, description
- impact: { interestSaved, monthsSaved, newClosureDate }
- priority: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'
```

Recommendations are sorted by interest saved (highest first).

---

### 6. OWNER'S WISHLIST (from note.txt)

**File:** `/Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/note.txt`

The owner envisions these future features:

1. **Loan Health Score (72/100 example)**
   - Composite metric based on:
     - Interest rate vs market rate (comparing user's rate to RBI/market baseline)
     - Loan tenure (longer = less healthy)
     - Prepayment history (more prepayments = healthier)
     - Debt-to-income ratio
   - People love scores — this is high-value UX feature

2. **Smart Notifications**
   - Alert: "You can save ₹1.8L interest if you prepay ₹50k this year"
   - Market alert: "RBI reduced repo rate. You may qualify for lower interest rate"
   - Condition-based notifications (opportunity-driven)

3. **Multi-Loan Strategy Planner**
   - Support multiple loans (home, personal, credit card, car)
   - Prioritization strategies:
     - **Avalanche:** Pay highest interest rate first
     - **Snowball:** Pay smallest loan first
   - Show consolidated payoff timeline
   - Help users decide which loan to tackle first

4. **Loan Payoff Countdown**
   - Visual: "🏁 Loan Free Date: 15 July 2042"
   - Progress bar showing journey to freedom
   - "People love tracking progress"

---

### 7. KEY DATA FLOWS & ARCHITECTURE

- **Main component:** `App.tsx` orchestrates all loan data (form, prepayments, rate changes)
- **Hooks:** `useLoanData()` manages state; `useAmortization()` computes schedule; `useRecommendations()` fetches API recommendations
- **Simulation:** `WhatIfSimulator` uses same engine (`calculateAmortization`) to project alternative scenarios
- **Export:** PDF generation available with full schedule + summary cards

---

### Summary for Your Planning

**What's Already Built:**
- 6 data-driven charts covering balance, principal/interest breakdown, cumulative interest, yearly summaries, and scenario comparisons
- 8 summary metric cards with progress tracking
- 3 recommendation engines (prepayment, EMI increase, lump sum)
- What-if simulator with ROI calculation
- Full amortization schedule with rate change support

**Biggest Gaps to Fill:**
1. Loan Health Score (new metric, requires market data)
2. Payoff countdown + progress visualization
3. Multi-loan support (architecture change)
4. Smart notifications (requires new service layer)
5. Derivatives like interest burden ratio, breakeven month, savings trajectory

**Most Impactful Next Additions:**
- Loan Health Score (high engagement)
- Payoff countdown (high engagement)
- Market rate comparison insight
- Annual savings projection based on prepayment scenarios

## UI/UX Exploration Report: Loan Analyser

Based on my comprehensive analysis of the loan-analyser project, here are the findings:

### 1. ICONOGRAPHY PATTERNS

**Current Approach:** 100% inline SVG hardcoding (no external icon library)
- **No icon library installed** — package.json has no lucide-react, heroicons, or react-icons dependencies
- **Approximately 40+ inline `<svg>` elements scattered throughout** the codebase across multiple components
- **Icon distribution across components:**
  - SummaryCards.tsx: 8 unique inline SVGs (bank, shield, calendar, clock, chart bars, currency, pie chart, trending chart)
  - App.tsx: 6 inline SVGs (wallet icon, spinning loader, download arrow, error circle, notification circle, chat bubble)
  - LoanForm.tsx: 2 inline SVGs (document icon, chevron up/down)
  - ChatWidget.tsx: 2 inline SVGs (close X, chat bubble)
  - PrePaymentList.tsx & RateChangeList.tsx: Plus signs and edit/delete icons
  - InfoTooltip.tsx: Info circle icon
  - RecommendationPanel.tsx, WhatIfSimulator.tsx: Various header icons
  - AmortizationTable.tsx: Table icon header
  - Charts & PDF components: Additional SVGs

**Inconsistencies Found:**
- Icons are duplicated across components (e.g., plus sign icon appears in PrePaymentForm, PrePaymentList, RateChangeList independently)
- No shared Icon component or wrapper — each SVG is hardcoded with individual styling
- Inconsistent strokeWidth values (some use 1.5, some 2, some fill="none")
- Icon sizing varies (some h-4 w-4, some h-5 w-5, some h-6 w-6) — no standardized sizing scale
- Different icon styles mixed (some use stroke, some use fill)

**Files with inline SVGs:**
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/App.tsx (6 SVGs)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/SummaryCards.tsx (8 SVGs)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/LoanForm.tsx (2 SVGs)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/AmortizationTable.tsx (1 SVG)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/PrePaymentList.tsx (3 SVGs)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/PrePaymentForm.tsx (1 SVG)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/RateChangeList.tsx (4 SVGs)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/ChatWidget.tsx (2 SVGs)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/InfoTooltip.tsx (1 SVG)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/RecommendationPanel.tsx (3+ SVGs)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/WhatIfSimulator.tsx (2 SVGs)
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/components/charts/* (additional SVGs in charts)

---

### 2. STYLING SYSTEM & THEME

**Tailwind Configuration:**
- /Users/parth/Parth/Dev/Projects/loan-analyser/src/app/globals.css contains only `@import 'tailwindcss';` — minimal custom CSS
- Tailwind 4.2.1 with PostCSS plugin (@tailwindcss/postcss ^4.2.1)
- No custom theme configuration file found — using Tailwind defaults

**Color Palette Used:**
- **Primary gradients:** blue-600 → indigo-600 (used throughout buttons, icons, accents)
- **Status colors:** rose (red), emerald (green), violet, amber, orange, cyan, teal
- **Neutral palette:** slate (50, 100, 200, 400, 500, 600, 700, 900)
- **Semantic colors:** 
  - Error/Alert: red (red-50, red-100, red-200, red-400, red-700)
  - Success: emerald (emerald-50, emerald-100, emerald-600)
  - Warning: amber/orange (amber-50, amber-100, amber-300, amber-500, amber-600, amber-800)
  - Info: blue/indigo
  - Status: individual colors (rose for interest, emerald for savings, violet for closure, amber for months, cyan for total paid, orange for effective cost, teal for progress)

**Spacing & Sizing System:**
- Very granular Tailwind defaults (py-2, py-2.5, px-3, px-4, etc.)
- Rounded corners: xl, 2xl, lg, md, full
- No custom spacing tokens defined
- Border radii consistent: rounded-lg (10px), rounded-xl (12px), rounded-2xl (16px), rounded-full

---

### 3. RESPONSIVENESS PATTERNS

**Responsive Breakpoints Used:** sm (640px) and lg (1024px)
- **57+ responsive classes found** across components (sm:, md:, lg: prefixes)

**Good Responsive Coverage:**
- Grid layouts properly responsive: `grid grid-cols-2 gap-3 sm:gap-4 lg:grid-cols-4` (SummaryCards)
- Charts use `useIsMobile()` hook (custom mobile detection at 640px) to adjust heights, margins, font sizes
- Forms: `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3` (LoanForm)
- Padding/spacing scales: `px-3 sm:px-6 lg:px-8`
- Font sizing: `text-xs sm:text-sm`, `text-lg sm:text-2xl`
- Visibility toggles: `hidden sm:block` for subtitle in header

**Responsiveness Issues:**

1. **AmortizationTable — Major Issue:**
   - Uses `overflow-x-auto` for horizontal scrolling on mobile ✓ (correct pattern)
   - BUT: Table has many columns (Date, Rate, Opening, Interest, Principal, Pre-Pay, Total, Cum. Interest, Cum. Principal, Closing)
   - Text size is fixed at `text-sm` with no mobile optimization
   - Column padding is `px-3` or `px-4` — not reduced on mobile
   - On small phones, text will be unreadable; columns will be extremely cramped
   - No column hiding/collapsing strategy for mobile

2. **ChatWidget Panel:**
   - `sm:h-auto` but `h-full` on mobile — might expand unexpectedly
   - Fixed positioning `bottom-5 right-5` — good
   - But panel height might not be optimal on very small screens

3. **Charts:**
   - Responsive container height: 260px mobile vs 350px desktop ✓
   - Mobile margins reduced: `{ left: -10, right: 5, top: 5, bottom: 5 }` ✓
   - BUT: Some charts may still have crowded legend text on small phones

4. **Summary Cards:**
   - Good: `grid-cols-2 gap-3 sm:gap-4 lg:grid-cols-4`
   - Issue: On mobile, 2 columns might cause text truncation in card labels
   - Icon sizes: `h-6 w-6 sm:h-8 sm:w-8` — gap between mobile/tablet could be smoother

5. **Header/Footer:**
   - Header padding: `px-3 sm:px-6 lg:px-8` ✓ (responsive)
   - Font scaling: `text-lg` for title (no mobile reduction)
   - Subtitle: `hidden sm:block` (good UX, hidden on mobile)
   - Footer: flexes but might wrap awkwardly on extra small screens

6. **Missing md: breakpoints:**
   - Most components jump from sm (640px) to lg (1024px)
   - Tablet devices at 768px-900px may not have optimized layouts
   - Could benefit from intermediate sm:, md:, lg: progression

---

### 4. COMPONENT INVENTORY

**Main Components (src/components/):**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| LoanForm.tsx | Collapsible form to input principal, rate, EMI, start date; allows toggle to edit |
| SummaryCards.tsx | 8-card grid showing metrics: total interest, interest saved, closure date, months saved, total paid, effective cost, interest ratio, progress |
| AmortizationTable.tsx | Responsive table displaying full amortization schedule with month, date, interest, principal, pre-payment, closing balance |
| ChatWidget.tsx | Floating chat button (bottom-right) that opens AI assistant panel; receives loan data context |
| PrePaymentList.tsx | List of pre-payments with add/edit/remove functionality; shows date + amount |
| PrePaymentForm.tsx | Form to add new pre-payment (date + amount input) |
| RateChangeList.tsx | List of rate changes with add/edit/remove; shows effective date + new rate |
| WhatIfSimulator.tsx | Collapsible "what-if" panel to plan future pre-payments and visualize impact |
| RecommendationPanel.tsx | Collapsible panel displaying AI-generated smart recommendations (prepayment, EMI increase, lump sum timing) |
| CookieConsent.tsx | Privacy notice banner shown once on first visit; stores consent in localStorage |
| InfoTooltip.tsx | Small info icon that shows tooltip on hover/click (reusable across cards) |

**Chart Components (src/components/charts/):**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| BalanceChart.tsx | Line chart showing outstanding balance over months; compares actual vs simulated |
| CumulativeInterestChart.tsx | Line chart of cumulative interest paid over time |
| ComparisonChart.tsx | Bar chart comparing actual vs simulated scenarios side-by-side |
| PaymentBreakupChart.tsx | Pie/donut chart showing principal vs interest breakdown |
| PrincipalInterestChart.tsx | Stacked bar chart of principal & interest components per month |
| YearlySummaryChart.tsx | Yearly aggregation chart (if applicable) |

**PDF Component (src/components/pdf/):**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| PdfReport.tsx | Generates downloadable PDF report with all loan analysis data |

---

### 5. LAYOUT & SHELL

**Header (from App.tsx):**
- Fixed sticky header with `z-30` and backdrop blur
- Contains: Logo (gradient blue-indigo square icon), "Loan Analyser" title, subtitle "Smart insights for your loan" (hidden on mobile)
- Right side: "Export PDF" button (only shown after loan is entered)
- Padding: responsive `px-3 sm:px-6 lg:px-8`
- Background: white with 80% opacity + backdrop blur for glass effect

**Main Layout (App.tsx):**
- Background: gradient `from-slate-50 via-white to-blue-50/30` (subtle gradient)
- Max width: `max-w-7xl` centered
- Padding: `px-3 sm:px-6 lg:px-8` (responsive)
- Vertical spacing: `py-5 sm:py-8` and `space-y-5 sm:space-y-8`
- Grid layouts: `grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:gap-6 lg:grid-cols-2` (for charts)

**Footer (from App.tsx):**
- Border-top with slate-200
- Contains: Suggestions link, Privacy Policy link, Terms link, disclaimer text
- Responsive flex: `flex-col sm:flex-row` with gap adjustments
- Padding: `py-6` with horizontal padding matching header

**Chat Widget (ChatWidget.tsx):**
- Floating button: fixed position `bottom-5 right-5 z-50`
- Dimensions: `h-14 w-14` default, `h-12 w-12 sm:h-14 sm:w-14` when open (barely responsive)
- Colors: Gradient blue when closed, slate when open
- Panel: Opens as modal above button with custom sizing and overflow handling

**Layout (src/app/layout.tsx):**
- Uses Next.js 15 App Router
- No custom fonts specified (using system defaults)
- Minimal shell: just HTML body with children, CookieConsent, and Vercel Analytics
- Metadata includes SEO tags and schema.org JSON-LD

---

### 6. KEY UI/UX OBSERVATIONS

**Strengths:**
- Consistent use of Tailwind for styling (no random inline styles)
- Good use of color gradients for visual hierarchy
- Responsive grid layouts for main content
- Accessibility touches: ARIA labels, semantic HTML (tablist, tabpanel)
- Smooth transitions and hover effects
- Clear visual feedback (button active states, loading spinners)
- Proper use of elevation/shadows for component separation
- Good use of badges and labels for status indicators

**Weaknesses/Inconsistencies:**
- **Inline SVG duplication** — plus signs, edit icons, delete icons repeated
- **No shared Icon component** — each SVG hardcoded with props
- **Icon styling inconsistent** — strokeWidth varies, no size system
- **Table not mobile-friendly** — many columns, small text on mobile
- **Missing md: breakpoints** — only sm: and lg: used
- **Colors scattered** — no design tokens file (could use CSS variables)
- **Font sizes not fully responsive** — some fixed at text-sm, text-lg
- **Chart responsiveness** — uses custom useIsMobile hook instead of responsive container
- **No dark mode support** — design is light-only
- **No component documentation** — all components are inline-heavy

---

## Recommendations for UI/UX Overhaul

This data provides a solid foundation for modernization. Key areas to improve:
1. Create a shared Icon component library (extract all 40+ SVGs into reusable components)
2. Define design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) in CSS variables
3. Improve table responsiveness with sticky columns or horizontal scrolling optimization
4. Add md: breakpoint utilities throughout for tablet optimization
5. Extract repeated icon/button patterns into utility components
6. Consider adding dark mode support
7. Create a component storybook or documentation site

input.content:
# Plan: Add loan analytics + UI/UX polish

## Context

The Loan Analyser already has a solid foundation: an accurate amortization engine (`src/utils/amortization.ts`) that is the single source of truth, 6 charts, 8 summary cards, 3 recommendation strategies, and a what-if simulator. The owner (`note.txt`) wants the tool to be easier for everyday users to *understand their loan*, plus a general UI/UX uplift and better mobile responsiveness.

This plan adds four user-friendly analytics that surface insights the engine already makes possible (no engine rewrite), migrates the 40+ duplicated inline SVGs to `lucide-react` for consistency, and fixes the weakest responsive spots (notably the amortization table on phones). Scope is **light mode only** (no dark mode), confirmed with the user.

Goal: a more insightful, cleaner, fully responsive site that builds and runs verified end-to-end.

## What we're adding (all confirmed with user)

1. **Loan Health Score** (0–100, with factor breakdown + tips)
2. **Payoff Countdown** (loan-free date hero + progress + time remaining)
3. **Key insight strip** (breakeven month, avg monthly interest, interest/day, % interest of total)
4. **Rate sensitivity mini-analysis** (impact of +0.5% / +1% rate, no extra input)
5. **Icons → `lucide-react`**
6. **Responsiveness polish**, especially the amortization table

---

## Part A — New analytics (pure, engine-derived)

### A1. New util: `src/utils/insights.ts`
Single cohesive module of pure functions. Reuses `calculateAmortization` and existing types. No mutation; returns new objects.

- `computeKeyInsights(result: AmortizationResult, loan: LoanInput)` → `{ breakevenMonth, breakevenDate, avgMonthlyInterest, interestPerDay, interestSharePct }`
  - **breakevenMonth**: first `AmortizationRow` where `principalComponent > interestComponent` (the crossover where you start paying down more principal than interest). Return its `month` + `date`.
  - **avgMonthlyInterest**: `totalInterest / totalMonths`.
  - **interestPerDay**: `totalInterest / (totalMonths * 30.44)`.
  - **interestSharePct**: `totalInterest / totalAmountPaid * 100`.
- `computeRateSensitivity(loan, prePayments, rateChanges)` → for deltas `[+0.5, +1.0]`, clone loan with `annualRate + delta` (immutable spread) and run `calculateAmortization`, compare `totalInterest` and `totalMonths` against the current `withPrePayments` baseline. Returns `[{ delta, extraInterest, extraMonths }]`.
- `computeHealthScore(loan, summary)` → `{ score: number (0–100), grade: 'Excellent'|'Good'|'Fair'|'Needs Attention', factors: {label, score, max, hint}[], tips: string[] }`. Weighted sub-scores (no income/DTI input available, so use loan-derivable signals only):
  - **Rate vs market** (35 pts): compare `loan.annualRate` to a `MARKET_RATE` constant (≈8.5%, defined in this file with a comment that it's an indicative India home-loan baseline). Lower rate → more points.

# Plan: Add loan analytics + UI/UX polish

## Context

The Loan Analyser already has a solid foundation: an accurate amortization engine (`src/utils/amortization.ts`) that is the single source of truth, 6 charts, 8 summary cards, 3 recommendation strategies, and a what-if simulator. The owner (`note.txt`) wants the tool to be easier for everyday users to *understand their loan*, plus a general UI/UX uplift and better mobile responsiveness.

This plan adds four user-friendly analytics that surface insights the engine already makes possible (no engine rewrite), migrates the 40+ duplicated inline SVGs to `lucide-react` for consistency, and fixes the weakest responsive spots (notably the amortization table on phones). Scope is **light mode only** (no dark mode), confirmed with the user.

Goal: a more insightful, cleaner, fully responsive site that builds and runs verified end-to-end.

## What we're adding (all confirmed with user)

1. **Loan Health Score** (0–100, with factor breakdown + tips)
2. **Payoff Countdown** (loan-free date hero + progress + time remaining)
3. **Key insight strip** (breakeven month, avg monthly interest, interest/day, % interest of total)
4. **Rate sensitivity mini-analysis** (impact of +0.5% / +1% rate, no extra input)
5. **Icons → `lucide-react`**
6. **Responsiveness polish**, especially the amortization table

---

## Part A — New analytics (pure, engine-derived)

### A1. New util: `src/utils/insights.ts`
Single cohesive module of pure functions. Reuses `calculateAmortization` and existing types. No mutation; returns new objects.

- `computeKeyInsights(result: AmortizationResult, loan: LoanInput)` → `{ breakevenMonth, breakevenDate, avgMonthlyInterest, interestPerDay, interestSharePct }`
  - **breakevenMonth**: first `AmortizationRow` where `principalComponent > interestComponent` (the crossover where you start paying down more principal than interest). Return its `month` + `date`.
  - **avgMonthlyInterest**: `totalInterest / totalMonths`.
  - **interestPerDay**: `totalInterest / (totalMonths * 30.44)`.
  - **interestSharePct**: `totalInterest / totalAmountPaid * 100`.
- `computeRateSensitivity(loan, prePayments, rateChanges)` → for deltas `[+0.5, +1.0]`, clone loan with `annualRate + delta` (immutable spread) and run `calculateAmortization`, compare `totalInterest` and `totalMonths` against the current `withPrePayments` baseline. Returns `[{ delta, extraInterest, extraMonths }]`.
- `computeHealthScore(loan, summary)` → `{ score: number (0–100), grade: 'Excellent'|'Good'|'Fair'|'Needs Attention', factors: {label, score, max, hint}[], tips: string[] }`. Weighted sub-scores (no income/DTI input available, so use loan-derivable signals only):
  - **Rate vs market** (35 pts): compare `loan.annualRate` to a `MARKET_RATE` constant (≈8.5%, defined in this file with a comment that it's an indicative India home-loan baseline). Lower rate → more points.
  - **Prepayment activity** (30 pts): scaled by `summary.interestSaved / withoutPrePayments.totalInterest`.
  - **Effective cost** (20 pts): from `totalAmountPaid / principal` (lower multiple → more points).
  - **Tenure** (15 pts): shorter `totalMonths` → more points (e.g. full at ≤120 months, scaling down to ~360).
  - Generate 1–3 actionable `tips` from the weakest factors (e.g. "Your rate is above market — consider refinancing").

All thresholds as named constants at top of file with brief comments.

### A2. New components (light, presentational; receive `loan`/`summary` props, compute via the A1 utils in a `useMemo`)
- `src/components/HealthScore.tsx` — score shown via a Recharts `RadialBarChart` gauge (Recharts already a dep) or a simple SVG arc; factor bars + tips list. Reuse `InfoTooltip`.
- `src/components/PayoffCountdown.tsx` — hero card: "🏁 Loan-Free Date" using `formatDateFull(wp.closureDate)`, years+months remaining from today, and a progress bar reusing the same `monthsCompleted/principalRepaid` logic currently inline in `SummaryCards.tsx` (extract that into A1 as `computeProgress(result, loan)` and reuse in both places to avoid duplication).
- `src/components/InsightStrip.tsx` — compact responsive row (grid) of the 4 key insights with icons + `InfoTooltip`.
- `src/components/RateSensitivity.tsx` — two rows ("+0.5%", "+1.0%") showing extra interest (`formatCurrency`) and extra months, with a short explainer line.

Use existing formatters: `formatCurrency`, `formatCurrencyShort`, `formatDate`, `formatDateFull` (`src/utils/formatters.ts`).

### A3. Wire into `src/App.tsx`
Inside the existing `{summary && loan && (...)}` block, add (order, top→down):
1. `PayoffCountdown` (hero, right under `SummaryCards`).
2. A responsive 2-col grid: `HealthScore` + `RateSensitivity` (`grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2`).
3. `InsightStrip` (full-width thin row) before the charts.

These are pure-client; compute via `useMemo` keyed on `loan/prePayments/rateChanges/summary` (mirrors the existing `simulatedResult` memo pattern). No new API routes.

---

## Part B — Icons → `lucide-react`

- Add dependency `lucide-react` (`npm install lucide-react`).
- Replace inline `<svg>` usages with named lucide icons, standardized sizing via `className` (e.g. `className="h-5 w-5"`). Representative files (pattern repeats across all):
  - `src/App.tsx` (header wallet→`Landmark`, download→`Download`, spinner→`Loader2 animate-spin`, error→`AlertCircle`, chat→`MessageCircle`).
  - `src/components/SummaryCards.tsx` (replace the 8 hardcoded `icon:` SVGs with lucide components, keep the existing `accent`/`iconBg` color scheme).
  - `src/components/LoanForm.tsx`, `PrePaymentList.tsx`, `PrePaymentForm.tsx`, `RateChangeList.tsx`, `ChatWidget.tsx`, `InfoTooltip.tsx`, `RecommendationPanel.tsx`, `WhatIfSimulator.tsx`, `AmortizationTable.tsx`.
- Keep new components (A2) on lucide from the start.
- Do **not** touch `src/components/pdf/` or `src/app/api/export-pdf/template.ts` SVGs — the PDF is server-rendered to static HTML and shouldn't depend on a React icon lib. Also leave SEO/`opengraph`/`icon.svg` assets alone.

---

## Part C — Responsiveness polish (light mode)

- **`src/components/AmortizationTable.tsx` (biggest fix):** keep `overflow-x-auto`, but make columns responsive — hide secondary columns on small screens via `hidden md:table-cell` (e.g. Opening Balance, Rate, Cumulative columns), always show Month/Date, Interest, Principal, Pre-Pay, Closing. Reduce cell padding and font on mobile (`px-2 sm:px-3`, `text-xs sm:text-sm`). Verify horizontal scroll still works for the full set at md+.
- **Add `md:` breakpoints** to the chart grids and `SummaryCards` so tablets (768–1023px) get an intermediate layout instead of jumping `sm`→`lg` (e.g. summary cards `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4`).
- **`ChatWidget.tsx`:** constrain panel height on small screens (`max-h-[80vh]`) and ensure the floating button + panel don't overflow viewport.
- Keep the existing slate/blue/indigo palette and gradient shell — polish spacing/typography consistency, don't redesign.

---

## Files

**New:** `src/utils/insights.ts`, `src/components/HealthScore.tsx`, `src/components/PayoffCountdown.tsx`, `src/components/InsightStrip.tsx`, `src/components/RateSensitivity.tsx`

**Modified:** `src/App.tsx` (wire-in + memos), `src/components/SummaryCards.tsx` (reuse `computeProgress`, lucide icons), `src/components/AmortizationTable.tsx` (responsive columns), `package.json` (lucide-react), plus icon swaps across the component files listed in Part B.

**Reused (not modified):** `src/utils/amortization.ts`, `src/utils/summary.ts`, `src/utils/formatters.ts`, `src/components/InfoTooltip.tsx`, types in `src/types/loan.ts`.

---

## Verification

1. `npm install` (picks up lucide-react), then `npm run lint` and `npm run build` — both must pass clean (TS `strict`).
2. `npm run dev`, open `http://localhost:3000`. Enter a sample loan (e.g. principal ₹50,00,000, rate 9%, EMI ₹45,000, start 2023-01-01) and add a pre-payment + a rate change.
   - Confirm Health Score renders with a sensible 0–100 value + factor breakdown + tips.
   - Confirm Payoff Countdown shows loan-free date, years/months remaining, progress bar.
   - Confirm Insight strip shows breakeven month, avg monthly interest, interest/day, % interest.
   - Confirm Rate sensitivity shows extra interest/months for +0.5% and +1%, and that numbers move correctly when the base rate changes.
   - Confirm all icons render (no missing/blank icons) and look consistent.
3. Responsive check via browser devtools: iPhone SE (375px), tablet (768px), desktop. The amortization table must be readable/scrollable on mobile; summary cards and charts reflow cleanly at the `md` breakpoint.
4. Regression: Export PDF still downloads correctly; AI chat still opens and streams; localStorage persistence still loads on refresh.
5. Report the dev URL and a short summary of what was added; note explicitly which checks were run in-browser vs. only build/lint.

# Plan: Add loan analytics + UI/UX polish

## Context

The Loan Analyser already has a solid foundation: an accurate amortization engine (`src/utils/amortization.ts`) that is the single source of truth, 6 charts, 8 summary cards, 3 recommendation strategies, and a what-if simulator. The owner (`note.txt`) wants the tool to be easier for everyday users to *understand their loan*, plus a general UI/UX uplift and better mobile responsiveness.

This plan adds four user-friendly analytics that surface insights the engine already makes possible (no engine rewrite), migrates the 40+ duplicated inline SVGs to `lucide-react` for consistency, and fixes the weakest responsive spots (notably the amortization table on phones). Scope is **light mode only** (no dark mode), confirmed with the user.

Goal: a more insightful, cleaner, fully responsive site that builds and runs verified end-to-end.

## What we're adding (all confirmed with user)

1. **Loan Health Score** (0–100, with factor breakdown + tips)
2. **Payoff Countdown** (loan-free date hero + progress + time remaining)
3. **Key insight strip** (breakeven month, avg monthly interest, interest/day, % interest of total)
4. **Rate sensitivity mini-analysis** (impact of +0.5% / +1% rate, no extra input)
5. **Icons → `lucide-react`**
6. **Responsiveness polish**, especially the amortization table

---

## Part A — New analytics (pure, engine-derived)

### A1. New util: `src/utils/insights.ts`
Single cohesive module of pure functions. Reuses `calculateAmortization` and existing types. No mutation; returns new objects.

- `computeKeyInsights(result: AmortizationResult, loan: LoanInput)` → `{ breakevenMonth, breakevenDate, avgMonthlyInterest, interestPerDay, interestSharePct }`
  - **breakevenMonth**: first `AmortizationRow` where `principalComponent > interestComponent` (the crossover where you start paying down more principal than interest). Return its `month` + `date`.
  - **avgMonthlyInterest**: `totalInterest / totalMonths`.
  - **interestPerDay**: `totalInterest / (totalMonths * 30.44)`.
  - **interestSharePct**: `totalInterest / totalAmountPaid * 100`.
- `computeRateSensitivity(loan, prePayments, rateChanges)` → for deltas `[+0.5, +1.0]`, clone loan with `annualRate + delta` (immutable spread) and run `calculateAmortization`, compare `totalInterest` and `totalMonths` against the current `withPrePayments` baseline. Returns `[{ delta, extraInterest, extraMonths }]`.
- `computeHealthScore(loan, summary)` → `{ score: number (0–100), grade: 'Excellent'|'Good'|'Fair'|'Needs Attention', factors: {label, score, max, hint}[], tips: string[] }`. Weighted sub-scores (no income/DTI input available, so use loan-derivable signals only):
  - **Rate vs market** (35 pts): compare `loan.annualRate` to a `MARKET_RATE` constant (≈8.5%, defined in this file with a comment that it's an indicative India home-loan baseline). Lower rate → more points.
  - **Prepayment activity** (30 pts): scaled by `summary.interestSaved / withoutPrePayments.totalInterest`.
  - **Effective cost** (20 pts): from `totalAmountPaid / principal` (lower multiple → more points).
  - **Tenure** (15 pts): shorter `totalMonths` → more points (e.g. full at ≤120 months, scaling down to ~360).
  - Generate 1–3 actionable `tips` from the weakest factors (e.g. "Your rate is above market — consider refinancing").

All thresholds as named constants at top of file with brief comments.

### A2. New components (light, presentational; receive `loan`/`summary` props, compute via the A1 utils in a `useMemo`)
- `src/components/HealthScore.tsx` — score shown via a Recharts `RadialBarChart` gauge (Recharts already a dep) or a simple SVG arc; factor bars + tips list. Reuse `InfoTooltip`.
- `src/components/PayoffCountdown.tsx` — hero card: "🏁 Loan-Free Date" using `formatDateFull(wp.closureDate)`, years+months remaining from today, and a progress bar reusing the same `monthsCompleted/principalRepaid` logic currently inline in `SummaryCards.tsx` (extract that into A1 as `computeProgress(result, loan)` and reuse in both places to avoid duplication).
- `src/components/InsightStrip.tsx` — compact responsive row (grid) of the 4 key insights with icons + `InfoTooltip`.
- `src/components/RateSensitivity.tsx` — two rows ("+0.5%", "+1.0%") showing extra interest (`formatCurrency`) and extra months, with a short explainer line.

Use existing formatters: `formatCurrency`, `formatCurrencyShort`, `formatDate`, `formatDateFull` (`src/utils/formatters.ts`).

### A3. Wire into `src/App.tsx`
Inside the existing `{summary && loan && (...)}` block, add (order, top→down):
1. `PayoffCountdown` (hero, right under `SummaryCards`).
2. A responsive 2-col grid: `HealthScore` + `RateSensitivity` (`grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2`).
3. `InsightStrip` (full-width thin row) before the charts.

These are pure-client; compute via `useMemo` keyed on `loan/prePayments/rateChanges/summary` (mirrors the existing `simulatedResult` memo pattern). No new API routes.

---

## Part B — Icons → `lucide-react`

- Add dependency `lucide-react` (`npm install lucide-react`).
- Replace inline `<svg>` usages with named lucide icons, standardized sizing via `className` (e.g. `className="h-5 w-5"`). Representative files (pattern repeats across all):
  - `src/App.tsx` (header wallet→`Landmark`, download→`Download`, spinner→`Loader2 animate-spin`, error→`AlertCircle`, chat→`MessageCircle`).
  - `src/components/SummaryCards.tsx` (replace the 8 hardcoded `icon:` SVGs with lucide components, keep the existing `accent`/`iconBg` color scheme).
  - `src/components/LoanForm.tsx`, `PrePaymentList.tsx`, `PrePaymentForm.tsx`, `RateChangeList.tsx`, `ChatWidget.tsx`, `InfoTooltip.tsx`, `RecommendationPanel.tsx`, `WhatIfSimulator.tsx`, `AmortizationTable.tsx`.
- Keep new components (A2) on lucide from the start.
- Do **not** touch `src/components/pdf/` or `src/app/api/export-pdf/template.ts` SVGs — the PDF is server-rendered to static HTML and shouldn't depend on a React icon lib. Also leave SEO/`opengraph`/`icon.svg` assets alone.

---

## Part C — Responsiveness polish (light mode)

- **`src/components/AmortizationTable.tsx` (biggest fix):** keep `overflow-x-auto`, but make columns responsive — hide secondary columns on small screens via `hidden md:table-cell` (e.g. Opening Balance, Rate, Cumulative columns), always show Month/Date, Interest, Principal, Pre-Pay, Closing. Reduce cell padding and font on mobile (`px-2 sm:px-3`, `text-xs sm:text-sm`). Verify horizontal scroll still works for the full set at md+.
- **Add `md:` breakpoints** to the chart grids and `SummaryCards` so tablets (768–1023px) get an intermediate layout instead of jumping `sm`→`lg` (e.g. summary cards `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4`).
- **`ChatWidget.tsx`:** constrain panel height on small screens (`max-h-[80vh]`) and ensure the floating button + panel don't overflow viewport.
- Keep the existing slate/blue/indigo palette and gradient shell — polish spacing/typography consistency, don't redesign.

---

## Files

**New:** `src/utils/insights.ts`, `src/components/HealthScore.tsx`, `src/components/PayoffCountdown.tsx`, `src/components/InsightStrip.tsx`, `src/components/RateSensitivity.tsx`

**Modified:** `src/App.tsx` (wire-in + memos), `src/components/SummaryCards.tsx` (reuse `computeProgress`, lucide icons), `src/components/AmortizationTable.tsx` (responsive columns), `package.json` (lucide-react), plus icon swaps across the component files listed in Part B.

**Reused (not modified):** `src/utils/amortization.ts`, `src/utils/summary.ts`, `src/utils/formatters.ts`, `src/components/InfoTooltip.tsx`, types in `src/types/loan.ts`.

---

## Verification

1. `npm install` (picks up lucide-react), then `npm run lint` and `npm run build` — both must pass clean (TS `strict`).
2. `npm run dev`, open `http://localhost:3000`. Enter a sample loan (e.g. principal ₹50,00,000, rate 9%, EMI ₹45,000, start 2023-01-01) and add a pre-payment + a rate change.
   - Confirm Health Score renders with a sensible 0–100 value + factor breakdown + tips.
   - Confirm Payoff Countdown shows loan-free date, years/months remaining, progress bar.
   - Confirm Insight strip shows breakeven month, avg monthly interest, interest/day, % interest.
   - Confirm Rate sensitivity shows extra interest/months for +0.5% and +1%, and that numbers move correctly when the base rate changes.
   - Confirm all icons render (no missing/blank icons) and look consistent.
3. Responsive check via browser devtools: iPhone SE (375px), tablet (768px), desktop. The amortization table must be readable/scrollable on mobile; summary cards and charts reflow cleanly at the `md` breakpoint.
4. Regression: Export PDF still downloads correctly; AI chat still opens and streams; localStorage persistence still loads on refresh.
5. Report the dev URL and a short summary of what was added; note explicitly which checks were run in-browser vs. only build/lint.

content.subject: Wire new components into App.tsx

# Plan: Add loan analytics + UI/UX polish

## Context

The Loan Analyser already has a solid foundation: an accurate amortization engine (`src/utils/amortization.ts`) that is the single source of truth, 6 charts, 8 summary cards, 3 recommendation strategies, and a what-if simulator. The owner (`note.txt`) wants the tool to be easier for everyday users to *understand their loan*, plus a general UI/UX uplift and better mobile responsiveness.

This plan adds four user-friendly analytics that surface insights the engine already makes possible (no engine rewrite), migrates the 40+ duplicated inline SVGs to `lucide-react` for consistency, and fixes the weakest responsive spots (notably the amortization table on phones). Scope is **light mode only** (no dark mode), confirmed with the user.

Goal: a more insightful, cleaner, fully responsive site that builds and runs verified end-to-end.

## What we're adding (all confirmed with user)

1. **Loan Health Score** (0–100, with factor breakdown + tips)
2. **Payoff Countdown** (loan-free date hero + progress + time remaining)
3. **Key insight strip** (breakeven month, avg monthly interest, interest/day, % interest of total)
4. **Rate sensitivity mini-analysis** (impact of +0.5% / +1% rate, no extra input)
5. **Icons → `lucide-react`**
6. **Responsiveness polish**, especially the amortization table

---

## Part A — New analytics (pure, engine-derived)

### A1. New util: `src/utils/insights.ts`
Single cohesive module of pure functions. Reuses `calculateAmortization` and existing types. No mutation; returns new objects.

- `computeKeyInsights(result: AmortizationResult, loan: LoanInput)` → `{ breakevenMonth, breakevenDate, avgMonthlyInterest, interestPerDay, interestSharePct }`
  - **breakevenMonth**: first `AmortizationRow` where `principalComponent > interestComponent` (the crossover where you start paying down more principal than interest). Return its `month` + `date`.
  - **avgMonthlyInterest**: `totalInterest / totalMonths`.
  - **interestPerDay**: `totalInterest / (totalMonths * 30.44)`.
  - **interestSharePct**: `totalInterest / totalAmountPaid * 100`.
- `computeRateSensitivity(loan, prePayments, rateChanges)` → for deltas `[+0.5, +1.0]`, clone loan with `annualRate + delta` (immutable spread) and run `calculateAmortization`, compare `totalInterest` and `totalMonths` against the current `withPrePayments` baseline. Returns `[{ delta, extraInterest, extraMonths }]`.
- `computeHealthScore(loan, summary)` → `{ score: number (0–100), grade: 'Excellent'|'Good'|'Fair'|'Needs Attention', factors: {label, score, max, hint}[], tips: string[] }`. Weighted sub-scores (no income/DTI input available, so use loan-derivable signals only):
  - **Rate vs market** (35 pts): compare `loan.annualRate` to a `MARKET_RATE` constant (≈8.5%, defined in this file with a comment that it's an indicative India home-loan baseline). Lower rate → more points.
  - **Prepayment activity** (30 pts): scaled by `summary.interestSaved / withoutPrePayments.totalInterest`.
  - **Effective cost** (20 pts): from `totalAmountPaid / principal` (lower multiple → more points).
  - **Tenure** (15 pts): shorter `totalMonths` → more points (e.g. full at ≤120 months, scaling down to ~360).
  - Generate 1–3 actionable `tips` from the weakest factors (e.g. "Your rate is above market — consider refinancing").

All thresholds as named constants at top of file with brief comments.

### A2. New components (light, presentational; receive `loan`/`summary` props, compute via the A1 utils in a `useMemo`)
- `src/components/HealthScore.tsx` — score shown via a Recharts `RadialBarChart` gauge (Recharts already a dep) or a simple SVG arc; factor bars + tips list. Reuse `InfoTooltip`.
- `src/components/PayoffCountdown.tsx` — hero card: "🏁 Loan-Free Date" using `formatDateFull(wp.closureDate)`, years+months remaining from today, and a progress bar reusing the same `monthsCompleted/principalRepaid` logic currently inline in `SummaryCards.tsx` (extract that into A1 as `computeProgress(result, loan)` and reuse in both places to avoid duplication).
- `src/components/InsightStrip.tsx` — compact responsive row (grid) of the 4 key insights with icons + `InfoTooltip`.
- `src/components/RateSensitivity.tsx` — two rows ("+0.5%", "+1.0%") showing extra interest (`formatCurrency`) and extra months, with a short explainer line.

Use existing formatters: `formatCurrency`, `formatCurrencyShort`, `formatDate`, `formatDateFull` (`src/utils/formatters.ts`).

### A3. Wire into `src/App.tsx`
Inside the existing `{summary && loan && (...)}` block, add (order, top→down):
1. `PayoffCountdown` (hero, right under `SummaryCards`).
2. A responsive 2-col grid: `HealthScore` + `RateSensitivity` (`grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2`).
3. `InsightStrip` (full-width thin row) before the charts.

These are pure-client; compute via `useMemo` keyed on `loan/prePayments/rateChanges/summary` (mirrors the existing `simulatedResult` memo pattern). No new API routes.

---

## Part B — Icons → `lucide-react`

- Add dependency `lucide-react` (`npm install lucide-react`).
- Replace inline `<svg>` usages with named lucide icons, standardized sizing via `className` (e.g. `className="h-5 w-5"`). Representative files (pattern repeats across all):
  - `src/App.tsx` (header wallet→`Landmark`, download→`Download`, spinner→`Loader2 animate-spin`, error→`AlertCircle`, chat→`MessageCircle`).
  - `src/components/SummaryCards.tsx` (replace the 8 hardcoded `icon:` SVGs with lucide components, keep the existing `accent`/`iconBg` color scheme).
  - `src/components/LoanForm.tsx`, `PrePaymentList.tsx`, `PrePaymentForm.tsx`, `RateChangeList.tsx`, `ChatWidget.tsx`, `InfoTooltip.tsx`, `RecommendationPanel.tsx`, `WhatIfSimulator.tsx`, `AmortizationTable.tsx`.
- Keep new components (A2) on lucide from the start.
- Do **not** touch `src/components/pdf/` or `src/app/api/export-pdf/template.ts` SVGs — the PDF is server-rendered to static HTML and shouldn't depend on a React icon lib. Also leave SEO/`opengraph`/`icon.svg` assets alone.

---

## Part C — Responsiveness polish (light mode)

- **`src/components/AmortizationTable.tsx` (biggest fix):** keep `overflow-x-auto`, but make columns responsive — hide secondary columns on small screens via `hidden md:table-cell` (e.g. Opening Balance, Rate, Cumulative columns), always show Month/Date, Interest, Principal, Pre-Pay, Closing. Reduce cell padding and font on mobile (`px-2 sm:px-3`, `text-xs sm:text-sm`). Verify horizontal scroll still works for the full set at md+.
- **Add `md:` breakpoints** to the chart grids and `SummaryCards` so tablets (768–1023px) get an intermediate layout instead of jumping `sm`→`lg` (e.g. summary cards `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4`).
- **`ChatWidget.tsx`:** constrain panel height on small screens (`max-h-[80vh]`) and ensure the floating button + panel don't overflow viewport.
- Keep the existing slate/blue/indigo palette and gradient shell — polish spacing/typography consistency, don't redesign.

---

## Files

**New:** `src/utils/insights.ts`, `src/components/HealthScore.tsx`, `src/components/PayoffCountdown.tsx`, `src/components/InsightStrip.tsx`, `src/components/RateSensitivity.tsx`

**Modified:** `src/App.tsx` (wire-in + memos), `src/components/SummaryCards.tsx` (reuse `computeProgress`, lucide icons), `src/components/AmortizationTable.tsx` (responsive columns), `package.json` (lucide-react), plus icon swaps across the component files listed in Part B.

**Reused (not modified):** `src/utils/amortization.ts`, `src/utils/summary.ts`, `src/utils/formatters.ts`, `src/components/InfoTooltip.tsx`, types in `src/types/loan.ts`.

---

## Verification

1. `npm install` (picks up lucide-react), then `npm run lint` and `npm run build` — both must pass clean (TS `strict`).
2. `npm run dev`, open `http://localhost:3000`. Enter a sample loan (e.g. principal ₹50,00,000, rate 9%, EMI ₹45,000, start 2023-01-01) and add a pre-payment + a rate change.
   - Confirm Health Score renders with a sensible 0–100 value + factor breakdown + tips.
   - Confirm Payoff Countdown shows loan-free date, years/months remaining, progress bar.
   - Confirm Insight strip shows breakeven month, avg monthly interest, interest/day, % interest.
   - Confirm Rate sensitivity shows extra interest/months for +0.5% and +1%, and that numbers move correctly when the base rate changes.
   - Confirm all icons render (no missing/blank icons) and look consistent.
3. Responsive check via browser devtools: iPhone SE (375px), tablet (768px), desktop. The amortization table must be readable/scrollable on mobile; summary cards and charts reflow cleanly at the `md` breakpoint.
4. Regression: Export PDF still downloads correctly; AI chat still opens and streams; localStorage persistence still loads on refresh.
5. Report the dev URL and a short summary of what was added; note explicitly which checks were run in-browser vs. only build/lint.

The dev server is running at **http://localhost:3000** — open it to interact with the new analytics.

## What was added

**New analytics (all engine-derived, no engine changes):**
- **Payoff Countdown** — loan-free date hero, years/months remaining, progress bar
- **Loan Health Score** — 0–100 radial gauge with grade, factor breakdown (rate vs market, prepayment activity, effective cost, tenure) + actionable tips
- **Rate Sensitivity** — extra interest & months if rates rise +0.5% / +1%
- **Insight Strip** — breakeven month, avg monthly interest, interest/day, % interest of total

New module `src/utils/insights.ts` holds all the pure functions; `computeProgress` was extracted there and reused by `SummaryCards` to kill duplication.

**Icons:** migrated every inline SVG across all components to `lucide-react` (App header, SummaryCards, ChatWidget, LoanForm, InfoTooltip, AmortizationTable, PrePaymentForm/List, RateChangeList, RecommendationPanel, WhatIfSimulator). PDF template and SEO assets left untouched as planned.

**Responsiveness:** AmortizationTable now hides secondary columns on small screens (`md`/`lg` table-cell), tighter mobile padding; SummaryCards gets a `md:grid-cols-3` intermediate step. ChatWidget already handled mobile full-screen + constrained desktop height.

## Verification
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm run build` — green, TS strict, no type errors
- Dev server serves HTTP 200 with no runtime errors

**Not verified:** actual in-browser interaction (no browser automation here) — please click through the new cards, an Export PDF, and the AI chat to confirm visuals/behavior on your end.

content.text:
Lint clean, build green. The dev server is still running with hot reload at **http://localhost:3000**.

Here's what I refined on the four new analytics, all within the site's existing slate/blue/indigo + multi-accent palette:

- **Payoff Countdown** — added soft decorative glow circles for depth, a frosted "Time Remaining" pill, ring-bordered icon that scales on hover, and a hover shadow lift on the hero.
- **Loan Health Score** — gradient rose→pink header icon, a colored grade pill in the header (Excellent/Good/Fair tinted to the score color), cleaner gauge center ("out of 100"), and tips wrapped in an amber callout box. Card lifts on hover.
- **Rate Sensitivity** — gradient orange→amber header icon, rows now highlight orange on hover, and the base rate is emphasized in the intro line.
- **Insight Strip** — switched from flat white cards to tinted accent cards (violet/rose/amber/cyan) that match SummaryCards exactly, with the same hover lift and icon scale-up.

All four now share the consistent hover interactions and depth used elsewhere on the site. Open the page and hover the cards to see it — please click through to confirm the visuals feel right to you, since I can't drive the browser from here.
